title: Rapid node fallback and GPU rolling repair — cheat sheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, on-call friendly cheat sheet for rapid triage and graceful recovery when a node (or GPU) starts failing, or when we need to do a rolling repair/add capacity. It prioritizes keeping inference lanes healthy and minimizing token loss. It's intentionally terse — use it during an incident and expand later for a formal playbook.

Scope:
- Single node or single-GPU failures that cause degraded capacity or pod restarts
- Planned rolling GPU replacement/firmware updates
- Fast capacity backfill after an OOM/hardware failure
Not for: datacenter-wide network partitions, full control-plane outages (separate SRE runbook).

Key principles (keep top of mind):
- Protect latency SLOs: prefer traffic fallback at routing layer over aggressive eviction of live pods.
- Prefer cordon + graceful drain with short grace periods; avoid mass eviction when the cluster has tight capacity.
- If a repair might take > 30m, trigger capacity backfill/scale-up early.
- Communicate early: update #sre-ops and the incident ticket with ETA and next steps.

Quick triage (first 5–10m):
1) Map impact: how many pods on the node? which models/routes? use: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep <node-name>
2) Check node status: kubectl describe node <node> and kubectl get nodes -o wide
3) GPU health: ssh to host (or use node exporter metrics) and run: nvidia-smi -q; check for ECC errors, Xid L1/L2 codes.
4) Check recent kernel messages: sudo journalctl -k -n 200 or sudo dmesg | tail -n 100
5) Check pod-level logs for crashes / OOMs (kubectl logs) and Redwood serving logs for token failures/trace ids.

Quick decisions:
- If node is flapping and pods keep restarting: cordon + drain planned replacement.
- If GPU reports physical error codes (persistent ECC, XID unrecoverable): plan physical GPU replacement or forced reimage.
- If this is a single transient driver crash with quick recovery: consider a soft reboot of GPU drivers (systemctl restart nvidia || modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia) and watch for recurrence.

Commands (common):
- Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
- Drain (safe): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
- Uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>
- List pods by node: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- Check GPU: ssh ops@<host> sudo nvidia-smi -q | egrep "(Error|Xid|ECC)"
- Quick smoke on serving: /opt/smoke-tests/llm-serving-smoke.sh --model small --route /v1/chat/completions
- Promote fallback route (if necessary): curl -X POST $ROUTER_API/promote?route=low-latency-fallback (internal)

Recommended graceful drain pattern (when capacity tight):
- 1) Cordon node.
- 2) Identify critical pods (route=production, SLA tier = high). For those, do not evict automatically; instead: annotate them with emergency-protect=true and use rollout/fallback.
- 3) For non-critical pods, drain with short grace-period (60–120s) to allow KV cache flush.
- 4) Validate that autoscaler has headroom; if not, trigger capacity backfill (see below).
- Note: if pods use large KV cache, prefer a staggered drain: cordon -> drain subset of pods -> observe latency -> continue.

GPU rolling repair checklist (high level):
- Pre-checks: confirm gate window, incident comms channel, spare GPUs/nodes available, tools and serial console access.
- Step 0: mark node as maintenance in cluster inventory and monitoring (tag in Datadog/Grafana).
- Step 1: cordon node.
- Step 2: attempt soft recover: restart drivers, rebind MIG instances (if applicable), reboot host if drivers stuck. Wait 5–10m and re-run smoke tests.
- Step 3: if soft recover fails, drain node (staggered if dense). Ensure pods are rescheduled; if rescheduling fails, trigger capacity backfill.
- Step 4: physical replace or reimage node. Follow hardware SOP if physical GPU replacement; else reimage with approved base image and validated driver/kernel combo.
- Step 5: run validation: nvidia-smi, run our per-node benchmark: /opt/bench/gpu-health-check.sh -> record perf numbers in incident ticket.
- Step 6: uncordon only once smoke tests and perf checks pass.

Capacity backfill (when to trigger):
- Trigger early if: >15% of cluster GPU capacity is reduced OR >10% increase in P95 latency observed tied to resource shortfall.
- Fast approach (cloud): use managed instance group scale or autoscaler: terraform apply -var='override_count=<N>' or gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize <group> <N>.
- Fast approach (bare-metal/private): allocate standby nodes from pool, or move nodes from low-priority pools. Call the on-call infra engineer to request hot-pool allocation.
- After backfill: validate routing, confirm pods scheduled and warmed caches. Evict least-critical pods first if capacity still tight.

Validation and acceptance tests (post-repair):
- Smoke test script pass (3 consecutive runs, 30s apart).
- Liveness & readiness probes green for all rescheduled pods.
- Key metrics: per-route latency p50/p95 and token success rate within 10% of baseline.
- Spot-check GPU perf: run small throughput test (20s) and compare to known baseline.

Monitoring & alerts to check during and after repair:
- Node exporter: GPU temperature, ECC counts.
- Kube events: PodEvicted, NodeNotReady, ImagePullBackOff.
- Serving metrics: token errors/s, request timeout rate, tail-latency.
- Autoscaler events and capacity change logs.

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Hardware vendor needed: if repeated physical ECC/XID unrecoverable AND spare pool < 2 nodes -> Page hardware team + account rep.
- Cross-zone outage: involve SRE manager and platform-eng immediately.
- Customer-impacting degradation (>1k requests/min failing or >5% overall error rate): open P0, notify CS and on-call product manager.

Post-incident notes (what to capture quickly):
- Root cause hypothesis and supporting evidence (logs, Xid codes, dmesg snippets).
- Time-to-detect, time-to-recover, time-to-restore capacity.
- Which rollouts or changes preceded incident (driver update, kernel, infra change).
- Any manual knobs used (eg route toggles) and duration.

Concise checklist for on-call (copy/paste):
- [ ] Identify node and list pods (kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>)
- [ ] Cordon node (kubectl cordon <node>)
- [ ] Attempt soft-recover (restart drivers / soft reboot) and run smoke tests
- [ ] If fail, drain node with short grace, stagger if dense (kubectl drain <node> ...)
- [ ] Trigger capacity backfill if >15% capacity lost or autoscaler not scheduling
- [ ] Replace/reimage hardware, validate (nvidia-smi & perf checks)
- [ ] Uncordon and re-run smoke tests
- [ ] Update incident ticket with actions, timings, and next steps

Notes to self / rough TODOs (for follow-up doc):
- Flesh out mapping of Xid codes -> quick action table (L1/L2 steps).
- Add automation: scripted staggered drain that honors route priority labels.
- Add standardized perf benchmark and threshold values per GPU model.
- Validate driver/kernel matrix per image and bake recovery AMIs with correct versions.

References & quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/example-infra/gpu-failures-playbook
- GitHub scripts: git@github.com:redwood/infra-scripts (gpu-health-check.sh, smoke-tests)
- Incident: JIRA-OPS-4123 (current ongoing)

If anything is unclear during an incident, ping @oncall-sre and @platform-eng with the short subject: "node-fallback <node> <short-symptom>" and attach dmesg & nvidia-smi outputs.

-- end of cheat sheet --
